tex_content.html:
Corollary
[Discreteness of non-elementary algebraic limits] 1. 9.1.8\group thurston.ch09.convergenceSource: thurston:page-0245 Let $\Gamma $ be countable and let discrete representations $\rho _i:\Gamma \to \PSL (2,\C )$ converge algebraically to $\rho $. If $\rho (\Gamma )$ has no abelian subgroup of finite index, then a subsequence converges geometrically to a discrete group containing $\rho (\Gamma )$; in particular $\rho (\Gamma )$ is discrete.
Proof

\sketch Use compactness of based thick manifolds to obtain a closed geometric limit. Its identity component is abelian by the small-subgroup theorem, hence is trivial because it contains the non-elementary algebraic limit.

□
